glossary.Oedema: Swelling caused by fluid collecting in the tissues.
glossary.24hr urine: A collection of all urine over 24 hours to measure total protein loss.
glossary.Ascites: Fluid collecting in the abdominal cavity.
glossary.Pleural effusion: Fluid collecting between the lung and chest wall, causing breathlessness.
glossary.Foamy urine: Frothy urine caused by large amounts of protein in it.
glossary.Diabetic nephropathy: Kidney damage caused by long-standing diabetes.
glossary.Lupus: Systemic lupus erythematosus: an autoimmune disease that can attack the kidneys, skin, joints and blood.
glossary.NSAID: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug such as naproxen or ibuprofen.
glossary.Naproxen: An NSAID painkiller; regular use can cause nephrotic syndrome.
glossary.Anti-PLA2R antibodies: Autoantibodies against the phospholipase A2 receptor on podocytes, the classic marker of membranous nephropathy.
glossary.HIV: Human immunodeficiency virus, the commonest cause of secondary FSGS.
glossary.Flank pain: Pain in the side of the body between the ribs and hip, over the kidney.
glossary.Pulmonary embolism: A blood clot that has travelled to the lungs and blocks a pulmonary artery.
glossary.Total T4: All thyroxine in the blood, bound and free; low here because its binding protein is lost in urine.
glossary.Urine dipstick: A bedside strip test of urine for protein, blood, glucose, leucocytes and nitrites.
glossary.Urine protein:creatinine ratio: A spot urine test that estimates daily protein loss without a 24 hour collection.
glossary.Albumin: The main blood protein, made by the liver, which holds fluid in the blood vessels.
glossary.Loop diuretics: Strong diuretics such as furosemide that act on the loop of Henle to remove fluid.
glossary.Steroids: Corticosteroids such as prednisolone that suppress inflammation and the immune system.
glossary.Prophylactic: Given to prevent a problem rather than treat one.
glossary.AKI: Acute kidney injury: a sudden fall in kidney function over hours to days.
glossary.Thrombosis: A blood clot forming inside a blood vessel.
glossary.Glomerular filtration barrier: The three-layer filter of the glomerulus: endothelium, basement membrane and podocytes.
glossary.Basement membrane: The thin sheet of matrix in the glomerular filter between endothelium and podocytes.
glossary.Plasma proteins: Proteins carried in the blood, such as albumin and clotting factors.
glossary.Interstitium: The space between cells in a tissue, where oedema fluid collects.
glossary.Lipoprotein: A particle of fat and protein that carries cholesterol and triglyceride in the blood.
glossary.Clotting factor: A blood protein that helps form a clot.
glossary.T-cell: A type of white blood cell that directs and carries out immune responses.
glossary.Permeability factor: A circulating substance that makes the glomerular filter leaky.
glossary.Foot processes: The finger-like extensions of podocytes that wrap the capillaries and form the filtration slits.
glossary.Autoantibodies: Antibodies that wrongly target the body's own tissues.
glossary.Intraglomerular pressure: The pressure inside the glomerulus that drives filtration.
